Subject: POC requirements: audit logs + key control questions

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team reviewed the features we discussed and has three blocking asks for the POC:

- Ability to provide a customer-managed key (BYOK/KMS) for data at rest encryption;
- Configurable audit log exports (events, actor, timestamp) retained for 365 days;
- SSO group mapping + SCIM provisioning to restrict who can create models / export logs.

Could you point me to any existing docs or tell me whether Redwood supports these today? If not, what is the expected timeline to get a limited POC-level solution in place?

I've attached the Acme security questionnaire with the numbered asks (ACME_Security_RQ_v1.pdf).

Appreciate any detail you can provide so we can move the POC forward this quarter.

Best,
Emily

Marissa / team — quick technical triage notes: 

1) BYOK/KMS: we don't have full customer KMS rotation integrated in hosted yet. Current options:
   - Dedicated mode (customer-dedicated infra) + our KMS bridge (requires onboarding, ~2-3 weeks minimal)
   - Envelope key approach: customer provides DEK wrapped by our RMK; we can accept a wrapped key for a short-lived POC with additional audit controls (low-risk, quicker ~1 week).

2) Audit logs: we support structured audit events (auth, request, model_version, token_count), and can export to S3 or push to SIEM. Default retention is 90 days; 365d retention needs storage config and a small billing/ops change (estimated 3-5 business days once infra ticket is scoped).

3) SSO/SCIM: we have SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in Dedicated and Private. Mapping groups to roles is supported in Dedicated. For hosted/standard accounts we'd need to enable a dedicated tenancy for Acme (security wants isolation).

Attachments: kms-support-matrix.xlsx (I listed current support surface).

My recommendation for a POC: offer a dedicated, isolated tenant with envelope-key acceptance + extended audit export to Acme S3 bucket. That minimizes code changes and keeps keys customer-controlled for the POC window. I'll open INF-2487 to track the infra config.

- Dev

Subject: Re: Fwd: POC requirements: audit logs + key control questions

Thanks Dev — +1 to the envelope-key POC approach as the lowest-risk path, but a few security guardrails we need before we sign off on any exception: 

- Audit log integrity: logs must be exported to Acme-controlled S3 (write-once or object lock preferred) and we need a sample schema and signed delivery timestamps.
- Minimum retention and access controls: if we extend to 365d, limit the retention only on the exported copy; our internal host should still enforce a shorter local retention.
- KMS key lifecycle: document how key wrapping happens, where any plaintext DEK is present (should be only in memory and never persisted).
- Contractual/insurance checks: legal needs to evaluate indemnity for using envelope-key POC.

Action items for product/infra: please produce a short (1 page) POC runbook with steps, data flows, and rollback plan. Security will review and provide conditional sign-off.

-Neha

Subject: ACME POC: proposed next steps (timeline & owners)

Emily — thanks for the clear asks and for sharing the questionnaire. Quick internal triage produced the following proposed path for the POC: 

1) Short-term POC plan (target 2–3 weeks):
   - Dedicated, isolated tenant for Acme (to meet isolation requirement).
   - Envelope-key acceptance: Acme supplies a DEK wrapped by their KMS (Redwood will not store plaintext keys; unwrap only in memory during startup).
   - Audit export: Structured audit events streamed to your S3 bucket; retention on exported copy set to 365 days (we will keep a 90d local retention).
   - SSO/SCIM: enable SAML + SCIM group mappings in the dedicated tenant to restrict access.

2) Deliverables / owners:
   - Infra & product runbook (Dev/INF-2487) — Dev Patel, ETA 5 business days.
   - Security sign-off & POC guardrails — Neha Kapoor, ETA 3 business days after runbook.
   - Contract/exception review — Laura Bennett (legal deals team) to confirm any required redlines.

3) Ask from Acme: please confirm you can provide the wrapped DEK, S3 write access config, and a list of admin accounts for SCIM mapping. Also share any legal contacts for redlines.

If this sounds reasonable I can schedule a 30 minute technical handoff call for early next week and start the infra ticket.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
